questions.question: Which five phases make up the corrective maintenance process?

options.A: Planning, budgeting, execution, settlement and closing
options.B: Inspection, notification, release, confirmation and billing
options.C: Notification, planning, control, execution and completion
options.D: Request, approval, procurement, withdrawal and settlement

questions.explanation: SAP workflows can control and partly automate this five-phase procedure.

questions.question: What happens in the notification phase?

options.A: Malfunctions and other requirements are recorded in a notification
options.B: Orders are created and the required material is planned
options.C: The order is checked for material availability and released
options.D: Partial steps such as time confirmation are executed

questions.explanation: Notifications can be accessed and processed through a list.

questions.question: What happens in the planning phase?

options.A: Malfunctions are recorded in a notification by the reporting employee
options.B: The required material is withdrawn and the order is executed
options.C: Orders are created and planned: steps to be performed, material needed and utilities such as measurement devices and cranes
options.D: The order is technically completed and settled by Controlling

questions.explanation: Planning is based on the reported requirements.

questions.question: What happens in the control phase?

options.A: Malfunctions are recorded in notifications and assigned to objects
options.B: The order runs through checks such as material availability and capacity planning, is put in process and the shop papers are printed
options.C: The order is executed and unplanned material is withdrawn
options.D: The partial steps of time and technical confirmation are executed

questions.explanation: The checks are important for the release of the order.

questions.question: What happens in the execution phase?

options.A: The order is checked for capacity and material availability
options.B: The order is technically completed and the costs settled
options.C: The notification is created by the reporting employee
options.D: The order is executed and the required material is withdrawn, even material not planned or reserved for the order

questions.explanation: Unplanned withdrawals are entered with reference to the order number.

questions.question: Which partial steps are executed in the completion phase?

options.A: Notification, planning and release of the order
options.B: Time confirmation, technical confirmation and technical completion
options.C: Availability check, capacity planning and printing shop papers
options.D: Material reservation, purchase requisition and goods receipt

questions.explanation: Settlement by Controlling can be performed before or after technical completion.

questions.question: Which options does a planner have to create a notification and an order for corrective maintenance?

options.A: Only create the order first and add the notification after completion
options.B: Only create the notification, since orders are created automatically
options.C: Only use the SAP GUI transaction; Fiori and mobile are not supported
options.D: Create a notification first then add an order; create an order with a combined notification; or use a Fiori malfunction report

questions.explanation: The notification can also be created via a mobile device.

questions.question: Who corrects the malfunction and who completes the maintenance order?

options.A: The reporting employee corrects it; the controller completes the order
options.B: The plant engineer corrects it; the purchasing group completes the order
options.C: A maintenance work center corrects it; the supervisor or maintenance planner completes the order
options.D: The maintenance planner corrects it; the work center completes the order

questions.explanation: The order is confirmed by an employee of the work center, the supervisor or the planner.

questions.question: What does preventive maintenance include, compared with reactive maintenance?

options.A: Overhauls at specific periods and inspections to repair worn parts before they cause failures
options.B: Repairs only after a malfunction has been reported by an employee
options.C: Maintenance schedules based on device and sensor data from machines
options.D: Maintenance that is performed only by external service companies

questions.explanation: Reactive means repairing after the failure.

questions.question: What does predictive maintenance additionally take into account?

options.A: Fixed overhaul periods defined in advance for every asset
options.B: Only the inspection records of the maintenance workers
options.C: Only the costs of previous maintenance orders
options.D: Device and sensor data from the machine to optimize schedules and predict failures more precisely

questions.explanation: It requires connecting business information with sensor data; the Internet of Things (IoT) supports this.

questions.question: Which mega-trend supports connecting business information with sensor data for predictive maintenance?

options.A: Blockchain
options.B: Internet of Things (IoT)
options.C: Robotic process automation
options.D: Quantum computing

questions.explanation: A digital twin of each asset gives insight for better business insights and collaboration across the supply chain.

questions.question: What is a maintenance plant?

options.A: The plant in which the operational systems of a company are installed
options.B: The organizational unit in which maintenance requirements are planned
options.C: The unit of capacity in which maintenance work is carried out
options.D: A section of a plant defined by production responsibility

questions.explanation: If maintenance is planned at this plant, it is also the maintenance planning plant.

questions.question: What is a maintenance planning plant?

options.A: The facility where the technical systems of the company are installed
options.B: The workshop in which the maintenance orders are executed
options.C: The organizational unit in which maintenance requirements are planned, from its own plant or from assigned maintenance plants
options.D: The place where the spare parts are stored by the planner

questions.explanation: Planners within a planning plant are defined by maintenance planner groups.

questions.question: Which organizational level is listed for Enterprise Asset Management?

options.A: Maintenance planning plant
options.B: Company code
options.C: Controlling area
options.D: Storage location

questions.explanation: Maintenance plants that do not plan their tasks are assigned to planning plants.

questions.question: How are the units of capacity in plant maintenance managed?

options.A: As maintenance planner groups assigned to the planning plant
options.B: As plant sections assigned to the plant engineer
options.C: As functional locations assigned to the equipment
options.D: As maintenance work centers assigned to the maintenance plant as workshops

questions.explanation: Work centers are the capacity units of maintenance.

questions.question: Who is the plant engineer?

options.A: The planner who belongs to a maintenance planner group
options.B: The person responsible for a plant section, coordinating production and maintenance
options.C: The worker who confirms the time on the maintenance order
options.D: The employee who reports the malfunction in a notification

questions.explanation: A maintenance plant can be subdivided into plant sections by responsibility for production.

questions.question: How can a maintenance plant be subdivided?

options.A: By cost center groups and profit center groups of the controlling area
options.B: By company codes and business areas of the enterprise structure
options.C: By functional locations and equipment records only
options.D: By location-based criteria such as site, building and coordinates, and into plant sections by production responsibility

questions.explanation: Locations subdivide a maintenance plant by location-based criteria.

questions.question: In plant-specific planning, where are maintenance measures planned and executed?

options.A: In a different plant that is assigned as the planning plant
options.B: In the same plant where the requirement occurs, with workshops and spare parts from that plant
options.C: In several plants that share the same workshops
options.D: Centrally in the company code of the enterprise

questions.explanation: One maintenance plant is assigned to one planning plant.

questions.question: What characterizes cross-plant planning?

options.A: Multiple maintenance plants are assigned to one planning plant, which handles planning, execution and spare parts
options.B: One maintenance plant is assigned to its own planning plant
options.C: Each maintenance plant plans and executes its orders itself
options.D: The planning plant only stores the spare parts of other plants

questions.explanation: Example: plant 1200 requires maintenance but another plant carries out all further functions.

questions.question: What are functional locations?

options.A: Records of the individual objects such as engines and pumps
options.B: Hierarchically ordered structures that represent a technical system, a building or a part of it
options.C: Documents that record the work performed for a notification
options.D: Plant sections assigned to a maintenance planner group

questions.explanation: They structure a technical system into units that are relevant to plant maintenance.

questions.question: According to which criteria can a functional location be structured?

options.A: Spatial, objective, and strategic
options.B: Financial, technical, and legal
options.C: Notification, order, and confirmation
options.D: Spatial, technical, and functional or process-oriented

questions.explanation: Examples: building 1 and 2; press frame and hydraulics; polymerization and condensation.

questions.question: When should functional locations be used to structure systems?

options.A: To plan the dates and budgets of a project for its WBS elements
options.B: To represent technical structures, record maintenance tasks for parts, store technical data and monitor maintenance costs
options.C: To post actual costs and revenues for customer billing
options.D: To define the capacities of work centers for production

questions.explanation: They also help analyze the effect of usage conditions on the likelihood of damage.

questions.question: How is a functional location identified?

options.A: Using a number range of ten digits defined in the controlling area
options.B: Using the plant number combined with the material number
options.C: Using a structure indicator made of a coding template and hierarchy levels, up to a maximum of 40 characters
options.D: Using a serial number assigned automatically for each equipment

questions.explanation: The coding template controls which characters may be used and how they are grouped.

questions.question: What do the hierarchy levels of the structure indicator define?

options.A: Which level ends at which character and the number of hierarchy levels the structure may contain
options.B: Which characters (letters or numbers) may be used for identification
options.C: Which organizational units are assigned to the functional location
options.D: Which equipment is installed at the functional location

questions.explanation: The coding template controls the characters that may be used.

questions.question: Which views does the master record of a functional location use?

options.A: General, sales, purchasing and accounting
options.B: Basic, storage, costing and work scheduling
options.C: General, location, organization and structure
options.D: Header, item, activity and task

questions.explanation: Organization covers account assignment (company code, cost center) and the maintenance planning plant.

questions.question: What does a maintenance notification header contain?

options.A: Information used to identify and manage the notification, valid for the whole notification
options.B: The spare parts that are required for the maintenance work
options.C: The tasks that are pending after the maintenance was executed
options.D: The settlement rule that determines who bears the costs

questions.explanation: Items determine the problem or damage; a notification can contain several items.

questions.question: What do activities document in a notification?

options.A: The activities that are pending and arose after maintenance
options.B: The work performed, which is important for inspections as proof that tasks were carried out
options.C: The planned costs of the maintenance task
options.D: The damage found on the reference object

questions.explanation: Tasks describe pending activities, e.g., creating a report.

questions.question: Which reference objects can a maintenance notification be created for?

options.A: A cost center, a profit center or an internal order
options.B: A vendor, a customer or a business partner
options.C: A WBS element, a network or an activity
options.D: A functional location, a piece of equipment (with or without assembly), or a material with a serial number

questions.explanation: A notification may also be created without a reference object, e.g., for an object not managed under a number.

questions.question: When can a notification be entered without an object number?

options.A: Never; every notification needs an object number
options.B: Only when the order is created before the notification
options.C: Only for notifications of the type activity report
options.D: When a malfunction report refers to an object not managed under a number, or a request refers to a new object for an investment program

questions.explanation: The view of the reference object can be configured per notification or notification type.

questions.question: A notification is entered for an assembly on a piece of equipment that is assigned to a functional location. What does the system transfer?

options.A: Only the data of the assembly
options.B: All relevant data of the equipment and the functional location
options.C: Only the data of the functional location
options.D: No data; it must be entered manually

questions.explanation: The hierarchy of the objects corresponds to the specified sequence.

questions.question: A maintenance notification is required to create a maintenance order. True or false?

options.A: False: a maintenance order can be created directly (e.g., a breakdown order)
options.B: True: the order always takes its data from a notification
options.C: True: otherwise no costs can be collected on the order
options.D: False: notifications are created only after the order is completed

questions.explanation: An order can also be created for a notification, for combined notifications, or automatically from a maintenance plan.

questions.question: From which source can a maintenance order be generated automatically?

options.A: A purchase requisition of a stock item
options.B: A budget release of a project
options.C: A maintenance item of a maintenance plan
options.D: A planned order from MRP

questions.explanation: An activity report can also be entered afterwards as a technical confirmation.

questions.question: Which elements are included in a maintenance order?

options.A: Header data, object list, order operation, material list, production resources and tools, settlement rule and costs
options.B: Project definition, WBS elements, network and milestones
options.C: Items, activities, tasks and damage codes
options.D: Sales area, shipping point, delivery and billing document

questions.explanation: The header data identify and manage the order.

questions.question: What does the object list of a maintenance order contain?

options.A: The spare parts that are used up when the order is executed
options.B: The tools and protective clothing that are not used up
options.C: The tasks and guidelines for who performs the work
options.D: The technical objects to be processed and the notifications, used when the same activity is carried out on several objects

questions.explanation: Notifications assigned via the object list are separable from the order again.

questions.question: Does the object list control the order?

options.A: Yes: it controls the work and costs of every listed object
options.B: No: no adjustment of work, history or cost distribution takes place through it
options.C: Yes: it updates the history of every listed object
options.D: Yes: it distributes the order costs to the objects automatically

questions.explanation: Customer exit IWO10027 can distribute order costs proportionally to the objects.

questions.question: What do production resources and tools in a maintenance order represent?

options.A: Spare parts that are required and used when the order is executed
options.B: Tasks that are necessary and the people who perform them
options.C: Costs that are estimated, planned and actual for the order
options.D: Resources required to execute the order but not used up, such as tools, protective clothing and trucks

questions.explanation: Spare parts belong to the material (component) list.

questions.question: What does the settlement rule of a maintenance order provide?

options.A: A list of the technical objects processed by the order
options.B: Information on who should bear the costs; it is proposed from the master record of the reference object
options.C: A description of tasks and who performs them
options.D: The reservations for the stock materials of the order

questions.explanation: It can be changed when the first settlement rule is maintained for the order.

questions.question: What happens to stock materials planned for a maintenance order?

options.A: They are reserved in the warehouse (reservation)
options.B: They are transferred to project stock
options.C: A production order is created for them
options.D: They are posted as a commitment on the order

questions.explanation: The reservation time can be set in Customizing.

questions.question: When is an availability check performed for the components of a maintenance order?

options.A: It is only performed after the order is technically completed
options.B: It is only performed after goods receipts are posted
options.C: It can be called when components are assigned and is performed automatically at release; the order can be released without availability
options.D: It is performed at release and the order cannot be released without it

questions.explanation: Planned goods issues refer to the reservation; unplanned ones to the order number.

questions.question: How are planned and unplanned goods issues entered for a maintenance order?

options.A: Planned with reference to the order number; unplanned to the reservation
options.B: Both with reference to the notification number
options.C: Both with reference to the purchase order number
options.D: Planned with reference to the reservation number; unplanned with reference to the order number

questions.explanation: The Material Where-Used List (IW13) shows which withdrawals were planned and which unplanned.

questions.question: What is the process for non-stock materials in a maintenance order?

options.A: Materials are reserved in the warehouse and withdrawn with a reservation
options.B: Purchase requisitions are generated (on save or release), converted to purchase orders assigned to the order, and goods receipts debit the order with the PO value
options.C: Materials are posted as stock transfers from another plant
options.D: Materials are charged to the cost center of the equipment directly

questions.explanation: Invoice differences are automatically credited or debited to the order.

questions.question: Which activities can only be performed after a maintenance order is released?

options.A: Creating the notification and assigning the reference object
options.B: Planning operations and assigning components to the order
options.C: Changing the settlement rule and the header data of the order
options.D: Printing shop papers, withdrawing material, booking goods receipts, entering time confirmations and completing a task

questions.explanation: At release the system also checks availability of materials and production resources.

questions.question: In which ways can the time for a maintenance order be confirmed?

options.A: Only individually for each operation by the work center
options.B: Individually per operation, collectively, overall completion confirmation, or via the Cross-Application Time Sheet (CATS)
options.C: Only collectively through the operation list of the order
options.D: Only via CATS entered by the supervisor of the plant

questions.explanation: Maintenance activities can be entered as activity reports or confirmation texts.

questions.question: What status do operations get after a partial completion confirmation?

options.A: CNF (finally confirmed)
options.B: TECO (technically completed)
options.C: NOCO (notification completed)
options.D: PCNF (partially confirmed)

questions.explanation: The order gets CNF when all operations are completely confirmed.

questions.question: Which status does a maintenance order get when all operations are completely confirmed?

options.A: PCNF (partially confirmed)
options.B: CNF (finally confirmed)
options.C: TECO (technically completed)
options.D: OSTS (outstanding tasks)

questions.explanation: Completion confirmations can be reversed if they were assigned to the wrong operations.

questions.question: What does the completion confirmation of an internal operation trigger?

options.A: A goods issue from the warehouse to the maintenance order
options.B: A settlement of the order to the cost center of the equipment
options.C: An internal activity allocation between the cost center of the work center and the order, calculated as work time times activity price
options.D: A purchase requisition for the external service

questions.explanation: The order is debited with the costs.

questions.question: What does the overall completion confirmation allow?

options.A: Confirming times, technical details, inspection rounds and counter readings for an order on one configurable screen
options.B: Confirming only the working times of one operation
options.C: Confirming only the goods movements of the order
options.D: Confirming only the activity reports of the notification

questions.explanation: Time confirmations and technical confirmations can be processed in the same way.

questions.question: Which status does a maintenance order get at technical completion?

options.A: CNF (finally confirmed)
options.B: PCNF (partially confirmed)
options.C: TECO (technically completed)
options.D: NOCO (notification completed)

questions.explanation: It means the maintenance work required for the order has been completed.

questions.question: What status identifies a notification with outstanding tasks?

options.A: OSTS
options.B: NOCO
options.C: CNF
options.D: TECO

questions.explanation: A notification with outstanding tasks cannot be completed until the tasks are finished, but its order can be completed.

questions.question: Which status does a completed maintenance notification receive?

options.A: OSTS (outstanding tasks)
options.B: NOCO (notification completed)
options.C: TECO (technically completed)
options.D: CNF (finally confirmed)

questions.explanation: The notification is locked for changes.

questions.question: Which changes can still be made online to a technically completed order?

options.A: Add new operations and assign new spare parts to the order
options.B: Create new purchase requisitions for additional material
options.C: Re-open the order by changing the order type
options.D: Lock or unlock it, set the deletion flag, enter outstanding goods movements, confirmations and invoice receipts, and change the settlement rule

questions.explanation: Purchase requisitions without purchase orders get a deletion flag; open reservations and capacities are closed.

questions.question: What happens when technical completion is reversed?

options.A: The order is closed and cannot be changed in any way
options.B: The order is deleted together with its notifications
options.C: All settlement rules of the order are removed
options.D: The order gets its previous status, capacity requirements and reservations are rebuilt and deletion flags of unconverted requisitions are reset

questions.explanation: The status TECO can be reversed if required.

questions.question: What is the maintenance order, from a cost perspective, at period end?

options.A: The final bearer of all costs of the maintenance task
options.B: A collector of all costs of the planning and execution phases, which are settled to the actual originator of the costs
options.C: A statistical object that never carries real costs
options.D: A cost center that allocates activities to other orders

questions.explanation: Settlement follows the allocation-by-cause principle.

questions.question: To which receiver are routine maintenance costs generally settled?

options.A: The cost center of the maintenance work center
options.B: The G/L account of the spare parts inventory
options.C: The profit center of the plant section
options.D: The cost center of the maintenance object

questions.explanation: The cost center must be specified as the receiver in the settlement rule.

questions.question: After the order is completely settled, what is the balance of actual costs on the order and on the receiving cost center?

options.A: Greater than zero on the order; zero on the cost center
options.B: Zero on the order; greater than zero on the cost center
options.C: Zero on both the order and the cost center
options.D: Greater than zero on both the order and the cost center

questions.explanation: The cost center is debited while the order is credited.
